meta.storyTitle: Install and upgrade release bundles with a private runtime

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Choose a1: one shared user-level installer/manager with bundle and dev delivery adapters. Install launched from either IDE runs the same public platform installer script interactively in a visible terminal; the script owns prompts and output. IDE-specific installation wizards and hidden background installs are excluded. Lifecycle, migration, runtime and privilege constraints remain shared and unchanged. Successful interactive installation hands the same terminal directly to the installed insrc TUI after daemon readiness; it does not finish at an idle shell.

ownedContracts.name: Installation and release identity
ownedContracts.purpose: One installation owns one selected delivery mode, zero or one active release and zero or one unresolved operation. Release identities are immutable; the controller metadata never stores application DB contents.

ownedContracts.name: Manager command and operation state
ownedContracts.purpose: A private-runtime command runner serves both IDEs when daemon is running, stopped or blocked. One OS-backed exclusive lock serializes all mutating operations per installation; controller records and bounded progress are shared across clients. Interactive install is invoked by the shared script in the terminal. The structured manager protocol remains for ordinary control/status; the IDE does not drive installation prompts through it. The 'install' action is reserved exclusively for the shared bootstrap/installer script executing inside the interactive terminal. VS Code/JetBrains adapters must never invoke ManagerAction.install directly or drive its prompts through this protocol; they only launch/focus the terminal and observe completion/readiness. The s1 LLD must state and enforce this caller restriction.

ownedContracts.name: Dependency report and consent
ownedContracts.purpose: Foundation contract separates required private Node, Ollama availability and advisory agent CLI detection from their platform implementations in s3; IDEs cannot infer consent from plugin updates.
ownedContracts.interfaceSketch:
interface DependencyReport { runtimeReady: boolean; ollama: 'ready' | 'installed-not-running' | 'missing' | 'unavailable'; ollamaInstallOffer?: { id: string; destination: string; version: string }; agents: { claude: boolean; codex: boolean; vibe: boolean }; recommendations: string[]; blockers: string[] }
interface DependencyDecision { offerId: string; choice: 'install' | 'decline' }

ownedContracts.name: Ordered upgrade hook delegation
ownedContracts.purpose: Owned by foundational s1 because delivery preparation, startup guard and s5 runner all require the same hook manifest. s5 implements execution. Hooks run in-process inside a candidate daemon migration-only process that exclusively owns data; manager and IDE never open LMDB/Lance.

ownedContracts.name: Local transport and explicit installation home
ownedContracts.purpose: All consumers resolve the same installation home and endpoint. Unix retains daemon.sock; Windows uses a per-user/per-installation named pipe. The manager's Node bridge supplies JetBrains Windows transport without changing application RPC payloads.

ownedContracts.name: Shared terminal installer launch
ownedContracts.purpose: Foundation-owned contract makes manual and both IDE installation entrypoints identical. IDE adapters only open/focus a terminal and invoke the same script; the terminal owns the interaction and durable operation state/readiness determines success. On successful install/readiness the shared script releases installation ownership and launches the installed TUI in the same terminal; failure/cancel does not launch it.

boundary.internal: Own the foundational manifest, controller/operation/consent/hook/transport contracts because every branch already depends on s1. Private implementation covers bootstrap, runtime/payload integrity, bundle preparation/publication, platform lock adapter and atomic install records. Later stories implement lifecycle, checks and hooks behind these contracts. The canonical scripts and interactive installer mode are shared with manual invocation and both IDEs; terminal prompts and durable results are part of this foundation. Include the selected release's installed TUI entry/assets in the payload and default successful interactive installer-to-TUI handoff. The s1 LLD must explicitly reserve ManagerAction.install to the shared terminal bootstrap script and forbid IDE-adapter invocation. DEF traceability: E20261123c3d71313:S001:FR001 and this story's DEF acceptance criteria apply unchanged.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Private dev checkout/branch sync, lockfile installation and native build preparation; returns the same immutable prepared candidate. It does not define a second lifecycle or migration engine. Include the selected release's installed TUI entry/assets in the payload and default successful interactive installer-to-TUI handoff. DEF traceability: E20261123c3d71313:S002:FR001 and this story's DEF acceptance criteria apply unchanged.

Private platform dependency detection, user-level Ollama installation and agent CLI recommendations. It implements foundational reports/consent and never auto-installs agent CLIs. DEF traceability: E20261123c3d71313:S003:FR001 and this story's DEF acceptance criteria apply unchanged.

Private daemon start/readiness, boot guard integration, shutdown drain/immediate exit and exit-completion launcher wrapper; transport is shared. No delivery sync/build on start and no signal/PID daemon control. DEF traceability: E20261123c3d71313:S004:FR001 and this story's DEF acceptance criteria apply unchanged.

Private ordered migration runner, daemon migration-only mode, blocked-state persistence, interrupted-run validation and explicit retry. Hooks alone choose data changes and recovery policy. DEF traceability: E20261123c3d71313:S005:FR001 and this story's DEF acceptance criteria apply unchanged.

Private VS Code native terminal open/focus/launch integration, duplicate-action handling and post-install reconnect. It invokes the shared script and leaves all install prompts/output in that terminal, including after failure. Existing ordinary lifecycle and upgrade-consent UI remains thin. Successful installation automatically enters the installed TUI in that same terminal; the IDE only reconnects/status-checks and does not require a second click. DEF traceability: E20261123c3d71313:S006:FR001 and this story's DEF acceptance criteria apply unchanged.

Private JetBrains native terminal open/focus/launch integration with the same script, stdin/output and post-install readiness behavior as VS Code; no independent wizard or hidden install. Preserve background activation/control and Windows IPC bridge for ordinary daemon operations. Successful installation automatically enters the installed TUI in that same terminal; the IDE only reconnects/status-checks and does not require a second click. DEF traceability: E20261123c3d71313:S007:FR001 and this story's DEF acceptance criteria apply unchanged.

Private isolated VM/runner fixtures, target matrix evidence and release qualification results, including real Windows named-pipe behavior and preservation of host v2 daemon. Terminal-install parity checks cover each IDE and manual invocation, paths with spaces/Unicode, missing terminal support, declined Ollama, Ctrl+C/close, duplicate windows, retained output and readiness-confirmed completion. Verify successful install enters TUI in the original terminal, install lock is released before TUI use, TUI exit leaves daemon running, and failure/cancellation never opens TUI. DEF traceability: E20261123c3d71313:S008:FR001 and this story's DEF acceptance criteria apply unchanged.

nonFunctional.performance: Targets: local read-only inspection/reachability <=3 seconds; activation never blocks IDE UI. Progress/phase changes emit within 1 second after state changes. Ready startup target <=15 seconds excluding dependency/model initialization; startup probe deadline 30 seconds. Default graceful wait 60 seconds with configurable user deadline; timeout reports uncertainty and never silently escalates. Downloads/builds/hooks have per-operation budgets and progress, not an arbitrary task retry loop.
nonFunctional.security: No elevated commands, global PATH edits, user credential capture, LLM calls for dependency detection or shell-interpolated actions. Verify payload/runtime digests and targets, reject archive traversal/symlink escapes and module paths outside candidate payload. Local endpoints are user-scoped, capability-protected where needed; bind operation/instance/release identity. Signing deferred and no cryptographic authenticity claim from unsigned digest metadata. No IDE prompt automation or credential/input capture; terminal launch preserves argument boundaries. User-visible script identity matches manual release assets.
nonFunctional.observability: Structured operationId/installationId/from-to identity, platform/runtime/digest, phase/hook/stage, duration and actionable error code. Bounded NDJSON to IDE, logs in installation home with rotation; no credentials/tokens or full migration data. Report explicitly which platform/native checks passed and which were unavailable. Interactive installation prints human-readable phases and errors directly in the terminal. The terminal is retained after completion/failure; its output is not scraped or treated as success evidence.
nonFunctional.durability: OS-backed mutation exclusivity plus atomic versioned controller records. Prepared payloads immutable; candidate data mutation is daemon-owned only. Record hook run-started before execution and require test before completion; failures/interruption retain blocked startup. Retry never substitutes a different candidate or starts the predecessor after data changes automatically. Installation completion and lock release precede the interactive TUI session. TUI exit/launch failure cannot roll back the completed installation or keep an installation lock held.

summary.prose: Story 1 supplies the release installer foundation: exact-target bundles, private Node, durable install records and the shared interactive scripts. IDE installation can only launch those scripts in a terminal; success enters the installed TUI after readiness and lock release. Actual daemon shutdown/readiness, migration execution and dependency discovery remain sibling implementations behind required ports.

api.name: ReleaseManifest
api.signature: interface ReleaseManifest { schemaVersion: 1; releaseId: string; sourceCommit: string; target: Target; runtime: RuntimeIdentity; payloadSha256: string; daemonEntry: string; managerEntry: string; tuiEntry: string; protocolVersion: 1; compatiblePredecessors: string[]; migrations: HookReference[] }

parameters.name: manifest
parameters.purpose: Untrusted standalone release descriptor and requested OS/arch/channel identity.

returns.meaning: Schema-validated immutable candidate descriptor; module-local installer type, unrelated to the design-corpus namesake.

preconditions: HTTPS artifact metadata; explicit configured repository/channel and target.
Manifest/schema, target baseline, entrypoint containment, unique ordered hooks, digest format and predecessor compatibility must validate.
postconditions: No candidate code is launched before archive and inventory integrity/target validation.
Archive digest is held in an external sidecar descriptor, never embedded self-referentially inside the archive.

errors.condition: Unsupported schema/protocol, malformed identity/path/digest, wrong target or predecessor.

api.name: Installation
api.signature: interface Installation { schemaVersion: 1; installationId: string; dataHome: string; delivery: Delivery; activeReleaseId?: string; operationId?: string }

parameters.name: record
parameters.purpose: Installation part of the controller snapshot; inspect never allocates an installation.

returns.meaning: Validated installation identity and selected delivery.

preconditions: Explicit absolute home; local supported filesystem; no symlinked control roots.
A mutating caller must hold the OS operation lock.
postconditions: Mode and data home cannot silently change during bundle upgrade.
Default home remains user ~/.insrc; explicit isolated home resolves consistently for all launched peers.

errors.condition: Unreadable/inconsistent state after enrollment; no silent reinitialization.

api.name: ManagerRequest
api.signature:
type IdeManagerAction = Exclude<ManagerAction, 'install'>;
interface ManagerRequest { protocolVersion: 1; operationId: string; action: ManagerAction; installationId: string; shutdownMode?: 'graceful' | 'immediate'; acceptedOfferId?: string; installOllama?: boolean }

parameters.name: request
parameters.purpose: Bounded structured request for ordinary control/status; install is forbidden on this IDE-facing input.

returns.meaning: Bounded progress or durable terminal result; all results bind operation and installation identity.

preconditions: Separate executable entrypoints: interactive installer and ordinary manager.
Ordinary manager input always rejects action=install, including caller/source flags claiming bootstrap origin.
Only the shared terminal script invokes the interactive installer entrypoint; stdin/stdout/stderr must be a TTY.
postconditions: IDE adapters cannot synthesize a source flag or submit an install action to bypass the terminal.
Interactive installer internally creates the install action; no cloud/DB/IDE runtime is loaded.
Unsupported sibling operations fail explicitly rather than using stub success.
Only same-operation escalation is forwarded before busy admission; the forwarder never writes controller state.

errors.condition: Install on manager protocol or non-TTY interactive entry.
Lifecycle/migration/dependency port not supplied by its owning story.

api.name: OperationRecord
api.signature: interface OperationRecord { operationId: string; predecessorId?: string; candidateId?: string; phase: Phase; hookId?: string; hookStage?: 'check' | 'run' | 'test'; errorCode?: string; message?: string }

parameters.name: record
parameters.purpose: State transition bound to installation lock and immutable candidate.

returns.meaning: Operation inside one versioned atomic controller snapshot with installation data.

preconditions: OS lock held; exact previous revision/phase/identity checked.
No destructive operation admitted without required peer capabilities and candidate compatibility.
postconditions: Single file replacement publishes active release and operation together; no independent active-selector file.
On ready/stopped completion release lock before TUI launch.
After disruptive uncertainty mark blocked; no automatic rollback or unbounded retry.

errors.condition: Request tries to resume another candidate or stale operation.

api.name: DependencyReport
api.signature: interface DependencyReport { runtimeReady: boolean; ollama: 'ready' | 'installed-not-running' | 'missing' | 'unavailable'; ollamaInstallOffer?: { id: string; destination: string; version: string }; agents: { claude: boolean; codex: boolean; vibe: boolean }; recommendations: string[]; blockers: string[] }

parameters.name: report
parameters.purpose: s3 supplies actual probes and user-level installation; s1 only renders prompts/results.

returns.meaning: Exact offer and explicit terminal choice returned to s3.

preconditions: No default-yes or IDE-filled consent.
Do not invent a report when s3 is unavailable.
postconditions: Coding CLI recommendations never install CLIs.
Declining Ollama remains visible; it does not become synthetic ready.

api.name: UpgradeHook
api.signature: interface UpgradeHook { check(context: MigrationContext): Promise<HookDecision>; run(context: MigrationContext): Promise<void>; test(context: MigrationContext): Promise<HookValidation> }

returns.meaning: Contract definition only here; s5 owns loading/execution and blocked-state policy.

preconditions: s1 validates reference shape, local containment, unique id/version and declared order.
s1 does not import/run hooks or open application databases.
postconditions: Candidate is not activated if required s5 migration service is absent, fails or returns unvalidated result.
Empty hook list still requires owning service to confirm no required migration; manager never assumes arbitrary state compatibility.

api.name: LocalEndpoint
api.signature:
interface LocalEndpoint { kind: 'unix' | 'named-pipe'; address: string; installationId: string }
interface InstallationLocation { home: string; installationId: string; daemonEndpoint: LocalEndpoint }

parameters.name: home
parameters.purpose: User default or explicitly selected absolute home.

parameters.name: installationId
parameters.purpose: Persisted installation identity; stable across release upgrades.

returns.meaning: Pure common path/endpoint resolver; peer implementations use this exact result.

preconditions: Reject unsupported/network controller filesystems, relative/traversal homes and overlong Unix socket paths rather than truncating.

api.name: TerminalInstallLaunch
api.signature: interface TerminalInstallLaunch { operationId: string; installationId: string; home: string; platform: 'posix' | 'powershell'; scriptPath: string; scriptVersion: string; scriptSha256: string; arguments: string[]; terminalName: 'Insrc Installation'; onInstallSuccess: 'launch-tui' }

parameters.name: launch
parameters.purpose: Canonical script identity and argument vector supplied to later native IDE terminal adapters.

returns.meaning: Durable operation phase plus exact IPC readiness, never scraped terminal output.

preconditions: Manual and IDE script bytes/version/digest match release assets.
Shared POSIX/PowerShell script bootstraps private Node, clears Node injection variables, and invokes interactive installer by absolute path.
IDE terminal open/focus and quoting belong to s6/s7.
postconditions: After valid ready result: persist installation completion, release operation lock, then run selected installed TUI with inherited terminal I/O and private runtime.
TUI launch failure is a post-install error with exact retry command; no reinstall/rollback.

api.name: escalateShutdown

parameters.name: input
parameters.purpose: Proposed additive HLD method input; validate unknown wire data before use.

returns.meaning: Identity-bound control outcome, never synthetic success.

errors.condition: Missing/stale owner or incompatible peer respectively.

preconditions: Approved HLD amendment; no application DB access.
postconditions: An immediate override during quiescing/draining is a message to the current operation, not a competing mutation. Invoke escalateShutdown with the existing installationId/operationId, action='stop', shutdownMode='immediate'. Before ordinary lock admission, the manager command forwards it to the current lock owner's user-protected local control endpoint. The owner remains responsive while awaiting drain/exit, validates recorded instance/operation and alone sends s4 IPC using its original completion endpoint/nonce and writes controller state. Cross-window requests use this path; duplicates coalesce; all independent mutations still return busy. Private endpoint discovery binds installation/operation/owner-session nonce, validates same-user authorization and phase/identity, and rejects stale endpoints. No lock release/steal to escalate. Missing/dead owner returns escalation-unavailable/uncertain; explicit recovery must acquire the lock and reconcile instance/exit evidence before acting, never automatically replace the daemon.

api.name: controlBridge
api.signature: controlBridge(command: { kind: 'send'; transportId: string; request: IpcBridgeRequest } | { kind: 'cancel'; transportId: string }): AsyncIterable<{ transportId: string; kind: 'written' | 'cancelled' | 'frame' | 'closed' | 'error'; written?: boolean; frame?: string; code?: string }>;

parameters.name: input
parameters.purpose: Proposed additive HLD method input; validate unknown wire data before use.

returns.meaning: Identity-bound control outcome, never synthetic success.

errors.condition: Missing/stale owner or incompatible peer respectively.

preconditions: Approved HLD amendment; no application DB access.
postconditions: The additive sc6 controlBridge envelope preserves existing inner frame types. Launch the helper explicitly in bridge-control protocol 2 and require version confirmation before sending; mismatch fails with no legacy fallback. Each send/cancel/event has a unique transportId bound to its embedded RPC request id and lane, never reused during helper lifetime. Validate before queue admission. A cancel processed before the first named-pipe write attempt removes the send, confirms cancelled/written=false and forbids later dispatch. At the first write attempt, mark written=true conservatively: possible dispatch, not application completion. A helper-stdin write is not pipe dispatch evidence. Post-write cancellation retires the local reply without rollback/replay promises. Helper death/lost outcome leaves unresolved sends unknown unless not-written was positively confirmed. Frame/error/close events carry transportId; report every pending id on lane failure where possible. Preserve 64-pending/16MiB aggregate bounds, fragmented UTF-8 and separate stream-lane cancellation. Input EOF closes the helper lane, never daemon.

api.name: bridgeHandshake
api.signature: bridgeHandshake(request: { kind: 'hello'; protocolVersion: 2; sessionNonce: string }): Promise<{ kind: 'ready'; protocolVersion: 2; sessionNonce: string }>;

parameters.name: request
parameters.purpose: Exact shared-contract identity input; validate untrusted wire data before use.

returns.meaning: Validated shared-contract evidence, not application success.

preconditions: Approved HLD amendment; owner implementation and consumer integration remain separate.
postconditions: The bridge-control protocol-2 startup wire exchange is exactly one UTF-8 NDJSON hello record {kind:'hello',protocolVersion:2,sessionNonce} from the client on helper stdin, then exactly one ready record {kind:'ready',protocolVersion:2,sessionNonce} on helper stdout. The client generates a fresh unpredictable sessionNonce per helper process; helper echoes it only after validating the version and binding its configured local installation endpoint. This is a separate startup envelope, not an IpcBridgeRequest and not a correlated controlBridge outcome; it has no transportId because no request exists yet. The helper must not forward any application frame before emitting ready, and the client must not send send/cancel records until matching ready is received. Set a 3-second handshake deadline from helper spawn; missing/malformed/duplicate/wrong-version/wrong-nonce ready, early outcome frames, or helper exit fail with bridge-protocol-mismatch/bridge-handshake-timeout before dispatch. On error the client closes stdin and that helper lane, reports no sends dispatched, and performs no automatic fallback/replay; it sends no daemon signal/stop. Unsupported hello yields only a bounded stderr diagnostic and helper exit without opening an application RPC lane. After ready, stdout contains only the specified correlated controlBridge events, stderr only diagnostics; later hello/ready records are protocol errors. Handshake bytes count toward the bounded parser/input limits; no credentials/capability tokens are echoed. Existing inner IpcBridgeRequest.protocolVersion=1 remains unchanged and is distinct from outer bridge-control version 2.

errors.condition: No matching ready within three seconds.
Malformed, mismatched or out-of-order startup record.

dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: interface ControllerSnapshot { schemaVersion: 1; revision: number; installation: Installation; operation?: OperationRecord; lastResult?: OperationRecord }
dataModelChanges.details: One small JSON file at <home>/install/controller.json owns installation plus current operation atomically; relative root notation is a proposed runtime layout. Write a same-directory unique temporary file with exclusive creation, flush contents, replace via platform atomic-replace adapter, then flush containing directory where supported. Never mutate controller.json in place. POSIX rename and Windows ReplaceFile/MoveFileEx semantics are isolated behind state module; qualify interrupted replacement on each filesystem. Serialize all writes under a persistent non-renamed <home>/install/operation.lock OS lock; no PID, heartbeat expiry or stale-lock unlinking. Inspection is read-only and returns missing versus corrupt distinctly. Existing application data is not copied or migrated by this record.

Release-owned Node 22.22.1 plus matching npm and current .npmrc headers are one policy. Pin exact official archive URL and independently recorded SHA-256 for each OS/arch; no latest or host Node fallback. Installed runtime path is <home>/runtimes/22.22.1/<target>. Bootstrap obtains official tar.gz on POSIX and zip on Windows using platform stock download/extract/hash facilities, verifies first, stages then publishes; if an extraction prerequisite is absent, fail with a user-level prerequisite message rather than sudo. Bundle contains the same official runtime archive so normal successor installs can reuse verified local bytes. Runtime extraction accepts only contained expected files; skip unneeded bin/npm aliases and invoke npm-cli.js through the private Node. Build/publish checks ensure .npmrc and runtime policy remain aligned. Shared source-development launcher is not silently rewritten as the installed launcher. Call sites here identify inspected publisher/launcher integration context, not existing consumers of this new model or instructions to edit those files.

Publish release.json sidecar with HLD ReleaseManifest, artifact URLs/sizes and digests for manager bootstrap assets and target lock binding; no hash refers to bytes that contain that hash. ZIP holds inventory.json of file paths/digests/sizes/modes, built out tree/assets, production dependency closure, single-file manager/installer bootstrap JS, native lock binding and the official private runtime archive. Content/root paths are bounded. Pure-JS yauzl reader is bundled into bootstrap JS; use lazyEntries, strictFileNames and validateEntrySizes plus our canonical-path, byte-count, entry-count and ratio limits. Reject absolute/UNC/drive/ADS/traversal/backslash ambiguities, duplicate or case-colliding paths, encrypted/unsupported entries, special files and symlink entries. Package builder dereferences only verified in-root workspace links; it never copies arbitrary host paths. Stage with exclusive creation and atomic same-filesystem publication. No end-user npm, compiler or daemon source build in bundle mode. Call sites here identify inspected publisher/launcher integration context, not existing consumers of this new model or instructions to edit those files.

Proposed source files: scripts/install.sh, scripts/install.ps1 and scripts/package-installer.mjs. A release-specific script embeds Node/bootstrap-JS/lock-binding digests; the tiny bootstrap JS is single-file bundled and uses builtin network/hash/fs plus its bundled ZIP reader. It downloads the separately digest-bound platform lock binding before acquiring the controller lock. This avoids requiring system unzip or host npm to read the full bundle. No payload/controller code runs before its digest matches. Bundle publisher emits identical installer bytes to manual assets and IDE resource staging; package root entrypoint managerEntry identifies this dependency-minimal artifact, not the whole application. Signing remains deferred; this provides digest/transport integrity only. Call sites here identify inspected publisher/launcher integration context, not existing consumers of this new model or instructions to edit those files.

s1 controller prepares candidate and owns durable installation transitions. It requires lifecycle/readiness (s4), dependency report/decision handling (s3), and candidate migration outcome (s5) through explicit peers. Those contract shapes are specified in this LLD's §2 and the HLD's shared contracts; this does not identify an existing source file. Their implementations are neither imported from hypothetical modules nor replaced with no-ops. Before any disruption, verify peer availability and exact candidate/predecessor compatibility. In the s1 build, deterministic peer fixtures exercise bundle orchestration; absent real peers produce capability-unavailable. Full live install/upgrade AC evidence remains contingent on sibling integration and s8; do not certify a real upgrade from fixture-only results. Dev preparation is a future s2 adapter, and native IDE terminal launch is s6/s7.

A minimal bundled Node-API v8 addon owns only an OS file-lock handle: nonblocking flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) on macOS/Linux; LockFileEx(LOCKFILE_EXCLUSIVE_LOCK|LOCKFILE_FAIL_IMMEDIATELY) on a fixed byte range on Windows. Keep the descriptor/handle alive, mark non-inheritable, release on close and process exit. Never rename/delete the lock file, and do not interpret file contents/PIDs as ownership. Deny lock-root symlinks and restrict user access; atomic-replace helper and user-SID lookup can share this small platform binding. It opens no DB, sends no process signal and is built/qualified in release environments, never compiled on client machines. Ongoing controller cancellation/exit must close handles; killed/crashed fixture cases are simulated by fixture self-exit commands, not daemon kill controls.

Invoke escalateShutdown with the existing installationId/operationId, action='stop', shutdownMode='immediate'. Missing/dead owner returns escalation-unavailable/uncertain; explicit recovery must acquire the lock and reconcile instance/exit evidence before acting, never automatically replace the daemon.

Only the lock-owning manager writes controller.json. Only the candidate daemon writes its operation/candidate-bound hook journal atomically while holding the exclusive data lease; it never writes controller.json or inherits the manager lock. Journal run-started commits before mutation. Stage events are advisory; OperationRecord is a possibly lagging projection, never migration validation evidence. Validate journal identity/version/order/digests before accepting results. On manager exit, a live candidate may finish its admitted hooks/journal but cannot activate or write controller state. A new lock owner first reconciles the exact candidate session, lease and protected observed-exit evidence; held/unknown ownership means busy/uncertain, never a second runner. Lease availability alone is not migration success. Only after prior candidate actual exit may explicit recovery validate the journal and resume the same operation or retry unvalidated hooks under hook policy. Reject stale session/revision writes; no PID/age inference or predecessor restart. Initial migration in migrating and candidate normal boot in activating require matching live-owner admission; independent ordinary boot remains denied. s4 owns lease/exit evidence; s5 owns hook execution/journal. Consume s4's approved mandatory migration receipt contract: manager records admission/session/nonce/path before spawn and validates receipt before recovery; receipt writing is wrapper-owned, not a controller.json mutation. Full receipt production/format is owned by s4.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Define strict manifest/location/runtime/installation schemas, immutable bundle preparation and identity/digest checks; add only internal sidecar/inventory metadata with no public contract rename.

Ordinary manager entrypoint rejects install unconditionally; terminal bootstrap entrypoint alone constructs it after TTY validation. One OS-locked atomic snapshot enforces operation transitions; peers are required and never silently successful.
Own report/decision types and terminal rendering; consume s3 implementation later. No Ollama installation or agent detection implementation in s1.
Own ordered reference/check-run-test types and shape validation only; s5 owns actual hook execution and migration failure/retry policy. Manager never opens DB.
Own explicit home/endpoint resolver and bridge envelope schemas. Existing PATHS/IPC adaptations and authenticated daemon transport are integrated by owning lifecycle/client stories.

Publish identical terminal installer scripts and launch descriptor; success commits ready state/releases lock before foreground TUI. Native IDE terminal open/focus/escaping is explicitly deferred to s6/s7.

errorCases.detection: Strict release/target validators compare requested OS/arch/baseline/protocol and installed predecessor before candidate execution.
errorCases.userImpact: Actionable unsupported target/release message; no source-mode fallback.

errorCases.detection: HTTP status/deadline/size counters, streaming SHA-256 and pinned control/runtime asset checks fail.
errorCases.response: Remove only operation-owned staging bytes; retain incumbent and retryable diagnostics.
errorCases.userImpact: No partial install is reported ready.

errorCases.detection: Prevalidated central directory plus canonical destination checks, exclusive creation, actual byte counters, inventory hashes and case-collision tracking detect invalid entries.
errorCases.response: archive-unsafe; do not execute extracted code or publish release directory.
errorCases.userImpact: No filesystem writes escape the staging root.

errorCases.detection: Absolute private Node reports different version/arch than policy or packaged native smoke probes fail.
errorCases.response: runtime-invalid before disruption; never fall back to PATH Node/npm.
errorCases.userImpact: Existing unrelated Node installations remain untouched.

errorCases.detection: Ordinary manager validates the request action before dispatch; install always fails there even with a forged bootstrap/source field.
errorCases.response: install-terminal-required; interactive installer additionally requires TTY on all standard streams.
errorCases.userImpact: User must use the shared terminal script; no hidden install or remote prompt driver.

errorCases.scenario: Controller missing after enrollment or unreadable
errorCases.detection: Schema validation/revision/installation linkage fails when selected state already exists.
errorCases.response: controller-corrupt and fail closed; do not recreate or select arbitrary payloads.
errorCases.userImpact: User gets explicit recovery diagnostics; data remains untouched.

errorCases.detection: OS nonblocking lock acquisition returns busy; lock contents/age are never considered.
errorCases.response: Independent mutation returns busy; same-operation immediate escalation forwards to the live lock owner under approved sc2.
errorCases.userImpact: Duplicate windows do not race upgrades.

errorCases.detection: Required handler admission fails before destructive phase; no fixture or implicit no-op is available in production.
errorCases.response: capability-unavailable. Internal peer handlers use s1-owned ManagerRequest/ManagerEvent/report contracts; s1 never imports or redesigns s4's shutdown implementation or s5's runner.
errorCases.userImpact: s1 alone cannot falsely report live end-to-end installation; later integration is explicit.

errorCases.detection: Abort signal/stream close or resumed preparing record with no quiescing admission.
errorCases.response: Retain error/result and clear only owned incomplete candidate staging under lock.
errorCases.userImpact: Incumbent remains usable; no TUI launches.

errorCases.scenario: Interruption after quiescing or during migration/activation
errorCases.detection: Durable phase/hook-stage record lacks successful completion/readiness; owning peer reports failure/uncertainty.
errorCases.response: blocked; retain exact candidate/predecessor and peer diagnostics. Only explicit retry can reconcile; no automatic predecessor start or rollback.
errorCases.userImpact: Ordinary startup stays blocked through sibling boot guard.

errorCases.scenario: Successful install but TUI launch fails
errorCases.detection: Ready result is already durable and lock released; installed private-runtime spawn or executable verification fails.
errorCases.response: post-install-tui-error with exact installed retry command. Do not change ready record or rerun installer.
errorCases.userImpact: Installation remains complete; terminal shows how to open TUI.

errorCases.scenario: Atomic state replacement or disk exhaustion
errorCases.detection: Staging/fsync/atomic-replace adapter reports OS error; reread validates whether old or new snapshot is authoritative.
errorCases.response: Before disruption preserve usable incumbent; after disruption retain/report blocked/uncertain state and avoid further writes until reconciled.
errorCases.userImpact: Never claim success from an uncommitted state transition.

errorCases.scenario: Manager exits while candidate hooks run
errorCases.detection: Owner control fails; explicit recovery validates controller revision, journal identity, candidate lease/session and observed exit.
errorCases.response: Follow sole-writer/journal reconciliation; never launch duplicate hooks or trust a lagging controller projection.
errorCases.userImpact: Safe explicit recovery without automatic activation/rollback.

alternativesConsidered.name: One versioned controller snapshot and immutable candidates
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Atomic installation/operation snapshot plus immutable release folders and a small typed set of sibling-service ports.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
Keep the HLD Installation and OperationRecord together in one schema-validated controller snapshot so selected release and operation phase change atomically. Manifests, target policy and immutable payloads are separate read-only inputs; an OS-backed lock serializes writes.

A bundle preparer and terminal-only interactive entrypoint return typed results. Lifecycle, dependencies and migration are required capability ports implemented by their owning sibling stories, not interchangeable plugin registries. Missing capability yields explicit unavailable/blocked results, not a successful partial install.

Both storage alternatives use operation-owner escalation and correlated bridge control only through the approved sc2/sc6 amendments; no permanent supervisor or second controller writer is added.
pros: One durable controller replacement avoids inconsistent active-release and operation files.
The type surface matches HLD contracts without an extra storage engine or service.
Failure and retry tests can exercise real filesystem state and explicit peer contracts.
cons: Readers must validate the entire small snapshot on every inspection.
s1 live install/upgrade acceptance still needs later sibling ports and target qualification; test peers are not native qualification.

alternativesConsidered.name: Append-only event journal with projected installation records
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Every phase transition is a durable event, with installation and operation views projected from history.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
Keep the same HLD public types but persist an append-only sequence of admission, preparation, cutover and completion events. Inspection replays events or reads a versioned projection to reconstruct Installation and OperationRecord.

The terminal entrypoint and bundle preparer use the same sibling capability ports. Journal replay, projection versioning and truncation policy become additional internal contracts even though no user-facing history feature was requested.

Both storage alternatives use operation-owner escalation and correlated bridge control only through the approved sc2/sc6 amendments; no permanent supervisor or second controller writer is added.
pros: Every state transition has a durable event history for diagnosis.
A failed projection can be rebuilt from valid journal records.
cons: Requires event compatibility, replay and compaction semantics beyond the requested small controller record.
Partial event tails and projection consistency add failure cases without removing the required OS lock or application migration ownership.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Technically viable, but event replay/projection lifecycle adds unnecessary internal contracts.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: The terminal script alone admits interactive installation, using verified private runtime/control assets. Candidate activation requires real sibling outcomes; only ready completion and lock release permit the same-terminal TUI handoff. Any missing or failed peer blocks this success path.
